launch: fresh isolated `claude -p` under sandbox-exec, --setting-sources '' --disable-slash-commands, --strict-mcp-config with ONLY the plumbline MCP server (remote Neo4j knowledge graph, HTTP), --allowedTools the 20 mcp__plumbline__* tools and --disallowedTools Bash,Read,Write,Edit,Grep,Glob,WebFetch,WebSearch,Task,...
cache_prefix_only_note: The first-turn cache read is the CLI's static system-prompt and tool-definition prefix, which is byte-identical across sessions on this machine and was warm from unrelated earlier sessions. It carries no case context: this run's own prompt shows up as cache_creation on that same turn, not as a read. So the RETRIEVAL measurement is clean; what is not comparable is the COST column.
cost_comparability_note: This run had prompt caching ON (cache_read=1,874,501), so its CLI cost is a cached price. Sibling arms on other cases were run both ways, so cost columns are only comparable within a caching mode. Re-run with DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1 for a like-for-like cost number; the ranked answer does not change.
cache_clean_note: cache_clean means no cache was inherited from an earlier session, which is what the run conditions require -- NOT that the run read no cache at all. In-run cache (the totals above) is expected and comparable. Judged on cache_read at the first assistant turn.
surface_pure_note: Arm surface is Opus 5 with ONLY the plumbline knowledge-graph MCP server (query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, get_community, god_nodes, graph_stats, shortest_path) against a single merged graph. Bash/Read/Grep/Glob/Write/Edit and every other MCP server are excluded by --disallowedTools and --strict-mcp-config, so a filesystem-grep escape was not merely unused but impossible. Any tool outside the plumbline allow-list counts as a surface violation.

sandbox.mechanism: sandbox-exec (macOS seatbelt), profile pinned at sandbox.sb
sandbox.gate4_verified_both_ways: before launch, the profile was proved to deny golden.json AND the pinned repo checkouts, while still allowing mcp_plumbline.json. Checking only unreadability is what let an earlier stale path pass a profile that denied nothing.
sandbox.note: The benchmark tree is denied wholesale and the ONLY re-allowed path is the single file mcp_plumbline.json (the MCP config the CLI must read to start). The pinned checkouts themselves stay unreadable -- this arm reaches code solely through the remote graph -- and golden.json and every sibling arm's results fail with EPERM. ~/.claude/projects is denied too, so no earlier session transcript - nor this run's own - is readable. cwd was a fresh empty directory, no settings sources were loaded and slash commands were disabled, so no CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins or hooks applied; auto-memory is unreadable under the sandbox.

prompt_caching: default (in-run caching allowed by this case's run conditions)

index.index_location: remote Neo4j knowledge graph via http://localhost/mcp
index.build: per-repo ingestion into a shared Neo4j graph spine; coverage and per-repo indexed commits read back from roll_call at finalize time (see index_coverage below)
index.index_repo_gap_note: index_repo_gap lists roster repos with NO knowledge row at all: gold in them is unreachable on this surface. index_commit_drift lists repos whose newest indexed commit differs from the pinned one; the pinned commit may still be indexed (indexedCommitCount>1) but is not the default snapshot. Neither list explains a miss in a repo that appears in neither.
